rationale: Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human or Parkinson's study isolates cold-pressed peanut oil on postural instability severity. Consistent with Rounds 1 and 5 (0/27 directional across prior peanut oil claims), peanut oil appears only as an omega-3 placebo comparator (ENHANce 2026, n=58, PD excluded) or an n-3-deficient mouse dietary comparator (Frances 1995, elevated rotarod null), while whole peanut butter (Feyesa 2026, standing balance null) cannot transfer to extracted oil. Safety caveats: crude/cold-pressed/unrefined peanut oil retains allergenic proteins capable of triggering acute IgE oral/throat reactions in peanut-allergic individuals whereas highly refined peanut oil was tolerated by 60/60 allergic adults (Hourihane 1997 PMID:9133891; Teuber 1997 PMID:9111495); deep-frying (190 C) and sunlight exposure generate cytotoxic alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes (Freis 2025 PMID:39942106); zero transfer from whole peanuts or peanut butter to extracted peanut oil.

Safety caveats: crude/cold-pressed/unrefined peanut oil retains allergenic proteins capable of triggering acute IgE oral/throat reactions in peanut-allergic individuals whereas highly refined peanut oil was tolerated by 60/60 allergic adults (Hourihane 1997 PMID:9133891; Teuber 1997 PMID:9111495); deep-frying (190 C) and sunlight exposure generate cytotoxic alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehydes (Freis 2025 PMID:39942106); zero transfer from whole peanuts or peanut butter to extracted peanut oil.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial has evaluated poached Pyrus pear on anxiety severity in Parkinson disease or any psychiatric cohort. The sole preclinical study (Anser 2021, PMID:34602398, n=10/group) gave a hydroalcoholic/ethanolic Pyrus communis fruit extract (200 mg/kg/d x 30 d) to healthy non-PD rats and mice and reported reduced forced-swim immobility and altered anxiety-maze scores vs distilled water, but a single unreplicated solvent-extract study in healthy non-PD rodents provides no defensible human PD bridge (exposure_fit=remote, population_fit=unusable). Human pear trials (Navaei 2019, PMID:30720034; Roh 2026, PMC13218835) assessed cardiometabolic/obesity biomarkers only, and PEARS antenatal lifestyle studies (PMC9286690) are non-food acronym exclusions. Matrix/safety caveats: raw Pyrus communis frequently triggers Bet v 1 pollen-food oral allergy syndrome in birch-pollen-sensitized adults (de Jong 2021, PMC8073155; heat-labile allergen denatured by poaching); high excess fructose and sorbitol FODMAPs can provoke bloating, cramping, or osmotic diarrhea in IBS/malabsorbers; strictly exclude prickly pear cactus (Opuntia ficus-indica), avocado pear, and PEAR/PEARS trial acronyms.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial or Parkinson disease animal model isolates poached Pyrus pear (P. communis / P. pyrifolia) on apathy severity. Systematic review (Reiland & Slavin 2015, PMC4657810) and subsequent human trials (Navaei 2019, PMID:30720034, n=40 MetS cardiometabolic biomarkers; Yang 2023, PMID:36856473, n=20 mild asthma PAH biomarkers; Roh 2026, PMC13218835, unripe extract obesity trial) assessed metabolic or respiratory markers with zero Parkinson symptom endpoints. Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial has tested raw Pyrus pear on baseline or Parkinson disease attention impairment. Although Lee 2013 (PMID:23587660, n=14 healthy young men) reported lower alcohol-hangover "trouble concentrating" (p<0.05) and memory impairment after Korean pear (Pyrus pyrifolia) juice given 30 min prior to 540 mL of 20.1% alcohol spirits, the mechanism was accelerated ethanol detoxification via ADH/ALDH stimulation (significantly lower blood alcohol, p<0.01) dependent on ALDH2 genotype—making that acute hangover model unusable for transferring to Parkinson attention impairment. Reiland & Slavin 2015 (PMC4657810) and Navaei 2019 (PMID:30720034) report no cognitive pear trials. Prickly pear cactus betanin mouse studies (Zietal 2025, PMC12524363) are botanically excluded. Matrix/safety caveats: raw Pyrus communis frequently triggers Bet v 1 pollen-food oral allergy syndrome in birch-pollen-sensitized adults (de Jong 2021, PMC8073155; heat-labile allergen denatured by poaching); high excess fructose and sorbitol FODMAPs can provoke bloating, cramping, or osmotic diarrhea in IBS/malabsorbers; strictly exclude prickly pear cactus (Opuntia ficus-indica), avocado pear, and PEAR/PEARS trial acronyms.

Remains Unknown (Researched): Despite pears containing ~6 g dietary fiber per medium fruit plus excess fructose and sorbitol, zero randomized controlled trials in adults or Parkinson disease have tested poached or raw Pyrus pears for constipation severity (confirmed by Reiland & Slavin 2015, PMC4657810; van der Schoot 2024, PMID:37905980; BDA 2025 Guidelines, PMC12623288). Pediatric fruit-juice crossover studies (Hyams 1988, PMID:3380601, n=20; Moukarzel 2000, PMID:10730921, n=39) documented breath-hydrogen carbohydrate malabsorption, diarrhea, and abdominal cramping after liquid pear juice in infants/children—not therapeutic constipation relief with poached pears in adults. Navaei 2019 (PMID:30720034, n=40 MetS) evaluated cardiometabolic markers without bowel outcomes. Anonymized Parkinson UK forum threads (#2386, #29143, #35031) are bundled and mixed (temporary relief alongside prunes/psyllium vs persistent constipation despite daily pears, plums, and laxatives). Cactus/prickly pear (Opuntia ficus-indica) nopal fiber IBS RCT (PMID:32935904) is a Cactaceae exclusion. Matrix/safety caveats: raw Pyrus communis frequently triggers Bet v 1 pollen-food oral allergy syndrome in birch-pollen-sensitized adults (de Jong 2021, PMC8073155; heat-labile allergen denatured by poaching); high excess fructose and sorbitol FODMAPs can provoke bloating, cramping, or osmotic diarrhea in IBS/malabsorbers; strictly exclude prickly pear cactus (Opuntia ficus-indica), avocado pear, and PEAR/PEARS trial acronyms.

Minimal directional signal that raw persimmon (Diospyros kaki)—specifically unripe, astringent, unpeeled, or heavily consumed fruit—can provoke acute epigastric/abdominal pain and gastric mucosal ulceration via diospyrobezoar formation, supporting the frozen "worsens" hypothesis as Maybe True (50.005). Zero human trials show raw persimmon relieves chronic pain. Conversely, causal human case-control and clinical cohort evidence links persimmon ingestion to painful ulcerative and obstructive gastric/intestinal bezoars: Benharroch 1993 (PMID:8409318, n=30 matched case-control: persimmon OR=9.8, unpeeled raw persimmon OR=56, p<0.01), Liu 2020 (PMC7549533, n=75 gastric bezoars among 23,950 exams, 25 persimmon/date-plum: 90.7% presented with abdominal pain, 90.7% gastric mucosal erosion, 60.0% gastric ulceration, 80.0% bloating p<0.001), Moriel 1983 (PMID:6825987, n=77 acute GI obstructions, 88.3% persimmon), Riaz 2024 (PMC10951130, n=31 symptomatic persimmon phytobezoars), Odeh 2024 (PMC11443479, healthy 35-yo with recurrent severe upper abdominal pain after unripe persimmons requiring laparoscopic extraction), Habuka 2025 (PMC12256139, 93-yo eating 2 persimmons/d with intestinal ulceration and obstruction), and Yonenaga 2026 (PMC13730816, 74-yo with persistent abdominal pain and ileal perforation from 98%-tannin bezoars). Parkinson disease gastroparesis/hypomotility creates direct host susceptibility to phytobezoar abdominal pain and ulceration (Ueno 2021, PMC8580754). Remains Unknown (Researched): No human clinical trial isolates raw culinary pineapple (Ananas comosus) on anxiety severity in Parkinson disease or other human populations. Hegelmaier 2020 (PMC7072275, n=16 PD) listed unspecified pineapple inside a bundled ovo-lacto-vegetarian inpatient menu without an isolated fruit contrast or item-level anxiety severity readout. Adu & Mabandla 2019 (PMID:31332728, already rated open in Round 1 0279) injected intraperitoneal pharmaceutical bromelain (40 mg/kg i.p.) into 6-OHDA rats without preserving striatal dopamine and does not transfer to culinary raw pineapple (and grilling denatures bromelain; Colletti 2024 PMC10974198; Ramli 2018 PMID:30381175). Cohort meta-analyses showing elevated PD incidence in pineapple plantation workers (Van Maele-Fabry 2012, PMID:22698719; Honolulu-Asia Aging Study) reflect occupational agricultural pesticide exposure rather than eating pineapple fruit, and 3D-printed levodopa printlets using chemically treated pineapple-leaf waste cellulose (PMC12899022) are pharmaceutical excipients. Critical matrix/thermal caveats: pharmaceutical bromelain pills are predominantly stem bromelain from inedible Ananas comosus stems (structurally distinct from fruit bromelain; Ramli 2018) and heat/grilling irreversibly denatures bromelain (Colletti 2024/2025); acidic/proteolytic raw fruit can irritate oral mucosa or trigger rare migraine/allergy flares, while high-dose bromelain supplements may interact with anticoagulants; exclude diagnostic B-SIT pineapple odorant studies and plantation-pesticide occupational cohorts.

Remains Unknown (Researched): Zero human clinical trials have tested whole culinary grilled (or raw) pineapple fruit on pain severity. Remains Unknown (Researched): Consistent with Round 1 pinto beans calibration (0/4 directional: R1 0273 insomnia, R1 0444 drooling, R1 0457 small handwriting, R1 0888 constipation — all open) and Rounds 2-5 bean/legume calibration, no controlled human trial or transferable Parkinson study evaluates whether cooked pinto beans reduces anxiety severity in Parkinson's disease. Human pinto bean RCTs assessed blood lipids, glycemia, fecal SCFA, and transient GI tolerance (Winham 2007 PMID:17634169; Finley 2007 PMID:17951475; Winham & Hutchins 2011 PMC3228670; Thompson 2012 PMC3489574; Johnston 2021 PMID:33347383) without evaluating anxiety severity, and Fox 2022 pooled generic beans inside whole-diet scores. Safety caveats: soak and boil dry pinto beans thoroughly (or use commercially canned beans) to denature raw phytohemagglutinin lectins, and introduce gradually to allow adaptation to oligosaccharide-related gas/bloating (Winham & Hutchins 2011 PMC3228670).

Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human trial has tested raw pomegranate arils on anxiety in Parkinson disease. The closest human clinical RCT directly measuring validated anxiety (Zare 2025, PMID:40808706, PMC12344722; 12-wk DB-RCT in 77 completed T2DM patients eating 3.5% pomegranate peel bread vs control) found ZERO between-group effect on DASS-21 anxiety (change +0.72 vs +0.89; p=0.81 unadjusted, p=0.92 adjusted). A 2023 systematic review (PMID:37640097) explicitly confirmed human anxiolytic clinical data are lacking (preclinical only), and a 2026 study flagged CYP3A4-mediated pharmacokinetic interaction between pomegranate juice and alprazolam (PMID:42489330). Concentrated pomegranate juice can inhibit CYP3A4 (e.g., alprazolam interaction, PMID:42489330; Chen 2018 review), rare pomegranate allergy is reported (PMC3354222), and preclinical rotenone rat PD studies conflict sharply (Tapias 2014 PMID:24315037 reported worsened nigral degeneration with commercial juice vs Kujawska 2019/2021 improvement with 6x concentrate).

Minimal directional signal (Maybe True, 50.005) that pumpkin seed protein-source tryptophan may ease anxiety, anchored by a small double-blind placebo-controlled crossover pilot RCT in social anxiety disorder (Hudson 2007, PMID:18066139; n=7 completed over 2 weeks with 1-week washout) where de-oiled Cucurbita gourd/pumpkin seed meal (22 mg tryptophan/g protein) paired with glucose carbohydrate significantly improved an objective anxiety measure during an anxiety stimulus whereas glucose alone did not. Preclinical mouse testing of ethanolic Cucurbita maxima seed extract (Wahid 2023, PMID:37006627, PMC10060065) reported anxiolytic behavior on EPM/light-dark tests, providing contextual animal support (not counted as a separate directional human signal because it tested an ethanol extract in healthy non-PD mice with a reporting error in statistical alpha thresholds). Kept strictly at minimal_signal due to tiny pilot sample size (n=7), non-PD social phobia cohort, proprietary de-oiled seed-meal + glucose co-ingestion (commercial patent conflict; differs from ordinary roasted whole pumpkin seeds), and abstract-only numeric reporting. Safety caveats: rare IgE-mediated pumpkin seed allergy (Paradis 2026, PMID:42231483), mechanical gastrointestinal/rectal phytobezoar impaction after heavy whole-seed intake (Cantor 2024, PMID:40026794; Gentile 2022, PMID:35910475 — pertinent in slow-transit PD constipation), mild GI upset, and protein/calorie load if eaten in large quantities near levodopa dosing.

Minimal directional signal (Maybe True, 50.005) for oral pumpkin seed oil on urinary urgency and frequency, anchored by a human monotherapy overactive bladder study (Nishimura 2014, PMID:24872936, PMC4032845; 45 enrolled, 38 non-BPH men and women analyzed) showing statistically significant 6-week and 12-week reductions across ALL four validated OABSS subscores (daytime frequency, nighttime frequency, urgency, and urgency incontinence) and total OABSS on 10 g/day oral Cucurbita maxima pumpkin seed oil. However, this easing signal is strictly weak and heavily tempered by four opposing or limiting clinical records: (1) Hong 2009 (PMID:20098586, PMC2809240; Korean quasi-randomized 4-arm BPH trial, 62 enrolled / 47 completed, 24% dropout, n=16 PSO 320 mg/day vs n=7 placebo) showed large within-arm PSO IPSS reduction (20.7 -> 8.7) and MFR advantage (+2.80 mL/s vs placebo in Benedicto 2026), YET reported NO statistically significant between-group differences across all BPH parameters at any timepoint; (2) Zerafatjou 2021 (PMID:34666728, PMC8527717; n=73 single-blind BPH RCT, 360 mg BID C. pepo PSO vs tamsulosin, no placebo arm) showed within-arm IPSS improvement (-3.19 pts, p<0.001, 0% AEs) but was statistically INFERIOR to tamsulosin (p=0.020); (3) Shirvan 2014 (PMID:25252490; n=100 BPH RCT, Prostafit PSO vs prazosin, no placebo arm) similarly showed within-arm IPSS improvement (-36%, 0% AEs) but was INFERIOR to prazosin (-44%); and (4) Benedicto 2026 (PMID:43018017, PMC13754250; SR/MA of 8 BPH RCTs, n=2,170) found sub-MCID 3m IPSS (-0.62) and NULL 6m pooled IPSS (+0.16, I2=84.3%). A completed cold-pressed PSO bladder pilot (NCT06944392, n=40, LURN-SI) has no posted results yet, and multi-herb formulas (Granu Fink femina, Femaxeen, Shim 2014 soy+EFLA 940) are excluded. Kept strictly at minimal_signal due to uncontrolled single-arm OAB design, C. maxima vs C. pepo species/cold-press uncertainty, non-PD cohort, and null/inferior BPH RCT comparators. Preclinical rodent data are conflicting and non-transferable to culinary boiled quinoa: Terreros 2024 (PMID:38337665 / PMC10857380) found that feeding 50% dehydrated raw white quinoa seeds to restraint-stressed adolescent rats had NO effect on anxiety-like behaviors (elevated plus maze and light-dark box), whereas studies reporting anxiolytic-like signals used non-culinary preparations—concentrated phytoecdysteroid/polyphenol extracts (Sidorova 2022 PMID:36558137) or live Lactobacillus kisonensis-fermented red quinoa supernatant in sleep-deprived mice (Ma 2026 PMID:42637361)—all in non-PD stress rodent models.

Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human trial, Parkinson cohort, or transferable animal study evaluates whether boiled quinoa reduces apathy severity in Parkinson's disease. Safety note: rinse quinoa thoroughly before cooking to remove bitter pericarp saponins.

Remains Unknown (Researched): Consistent with Round 1 quinoa motor calibration (R1 0215 walking slowness, R1 0405 muscle rigidity — both open), no human clinical trial, observational Parkinson cohort, or mammalian PD model evaluates whether boiled quinoa worsens bradykinesia severity in Parkinson's disease. Minimal preclinical directional signal favoring easing of anxiety-like behavior — opposing the frozen worsening hypothesis (Maybe False) — replicated across THREE independent animal laboratories and multiple species, including exact brewed infusion: (1) Pyrzanowska 2021 (PMID:33529651; Neuroscience Letters) administered chromatographically characterized hot-water infusions of fermented rooibos tea (1%, 2%, 4% w/v) as sole drinking fluid to adult male Sprague-Dawley rats for 3 months and documented increased central-zone occupation (reduced anxiety-like behavior) and head-dipping/rearing exploration in the hole-board test alongside lowered striatal glutamate/aspartate and elevated striatal/hippocampal taurine; (2) López 2022 (PMID:34877951; Food & Function) found unfermented green rooibos extract (GreenOxithin) produced significant anxiolysis in the larval zebrafish light-dark test, rescued GABA signaling in PTZ excitotoxicity, and moderately inhibited MAO-A; and (3) Valcarce 2026 (PMID:42104559; BioFactors) showed standardized green rooibos extract reduced anxiety-like behavior in both adult zebrafish (4-month feeding, Novel Tank Test, locomotion unchanged) and C. elegans (starvation octanol avoidance). Kept strictly at minimal_signal (50.005) because human clinical anxiety evidence is absent: Afrifa 2023 scoping review of all 18 human rooibos studies (PMC10774856, n=488) found zero powered human anxiety RCTs (only an exploratory emotional-domain trend p=0.09 vs coriander in osteopenic women), and Australian pilot ACTRN12626001145392 comparing lemon balm vs rooibos for GAD-7 anxiety is not yet recruiting. Zero human or animal studies show brewed rooibos worsening anxiety. Exposure boundary & safety notes: naturally caffeine-free, low-tannin brewed rooibos (Aspalathus linearis) is botanically distinct from Camellia sinensis green/black tea (no caffeine or L-theanine PD effects transfer, and rooibos does not impair iron absorption per Hesseling 1979). Rare clinical case reports document rooibos-associated hepatotoxicity (Sinisalo 2010 PMID:20072844; Engels 2013 PMID:26157822/PMC4435260 with buchu+statin; Reddy 2016 PMID:27871602; Carrier 2021 PMID:32828746; modest transaminase shifts in Marnewick 2011), and extracts inhibit CYP3A4/CYP2C19/CYP2C9 (Fantoukh 2019; rat atorvastatin AUC +5.9-fold in Patel 2019) — systemic hepatic/herb-drug cautions rather than direct worsening of the frozen PD symptom.

Minimal directional signal from non-PD oral clinical trials that dried rosemary eases rather than worsens anxiety, opposing the frozen 'worsens' claim (Maybe False) and paralleling Round 1 minimal_signal easing for rosemary depression (0128). Four independent oral rosemary RCTs in non-PD populations report anxiety reductions: Nematolahi 2018 (PMID:29389474, n=68 students, 1,000 mg/day dried rosemary leaf powder capsules x 1 mo -> HADS-Anxiety reduced vs placebo), Azizi 2022 (PMID:36343423, n=51 MDD completers on SSRIs, 1,000 mg/day dried milled rosemary leaf capsules x 8 wk -> HADS-Anxiety reduced vs placebo, noting baseline imbalance and 11/26 heartburn AE), Kuwata 2025 (PMC12646844, n=38 crossover, post-distillation rosemary residue extract -> 4-wk STAI Trait Anxiety 46.0 vs 48.2, p=0.014, and acute post-stress STAI State 46.0 vs 47.9, p=0.041, while 4-wk continuous STAI State was NULL p=0.153), and Heidarzadeh 2026 (methadone maintenance, HADS-Anxiety favored rosemary despite reporting discrepancies). Aucoin 2026 (local extract) found overall mixed-route anxiety inconclusive across 14 studies, while its planned oral-route subgroup meta-analysis favored rosemary (SMD -0.61, 95% CI -0.99 to -0.23). Opposing/null oral evidence: Araki 2020 (PMC7699484, hot-water extract, POMS Tension-Anxiety between-group p=0.171 NULL) and Kuwata 2025 continuous STAI-State (p=0.153 NULL). STRICT ROUTE EXCLUSION: All inhaled rosemary essential-oil aromatherapy trials (e.g., Moss 2003/2012, Sayadi Mank-Halati 2024, Can 2024) are excluded. Held at minimal_signal (50.005) due to zero PD anxiety trials, small heterogeneous cohorts, and partial nulls. Safety caveats: high heartburn rate (42% in Azizi 2022) and inverted-U cognitive impairment at high 6,000 mg oral dose in older adults (Pengelly 2012).

Remains Unknown (Researched): No controlled human trial isolates ordinary baked rye bread on anxiety severity in Parkinson's disease or clinical mood/sleepiness/fatigue populations. The closest controlled study, Sandberg 2018 (PMID:30400947 / PMC6220522, n=38 healthy middle-aged adults 52-70 y, 3-day evening crossover), reported higher next-morning Swedish Core Affect Scale VAS ratings for valence (pleased/glad/happy: +9% fasting p<0.05, +10% 0-180 min p<0.001) and activation (awake/active/peppy: +15% fasting p<0.01, +7% 0-180 min p<0.05) vs white wheat bread. Safety caveats: contains gluten (avoid in celiac disease) and fermentable fructans that can provoke gas/cramping in sensitive individuals.

Maybe True (minimal_signal, 50.005, toward easing): Four independent controlled human feeding trials demonstrate that whole-grain rye bread improves objective and subjective bowel motility versus refined white wheat bread or usual laxatives, though all studies enrolled non-PD adults and required high daily intakes with a documented FODMAP-driven GI symptom tradeoff. In Holma 2010 (PMID:20089780, n=51 constipated adults, 3-wk RCT), whole-grain rye bread (>=240 g/d) shortened total intestinal transit time by 23% vs white wheat bread (p=0.040) and 41% vs usual laxatives (p=0.006), increased weekly defecations by +1.4/wk (p=0.014), softened stools (OR 3.98, p=0.037), and eased defecation (OR 5.08, p=0.018) without increasing GI adverse effects. In Hongisto 2006 (PMID:16251881, n=59 women with self-reported constipation, 3-wk factorial RCT), fiber-rich rye bread shortened TITT (-0.7 d, p=0.007), increased stool frequency (+0.3, p=0.001), softened feces (p<0.001), and eased defecation (p<0.001), while increasing composite GI symptoms (+1.6, p<0.001; mitigated by LGG yogurt -1.3, p=0.027). Two additional randomized trials in healthy/overweight adults corroborate faster transit and higher stool frequency (Grasten 2000 PMID:10958815, n=17 crossover; Vuholm 2017 PMID:28954842, n=70 parallel, +0.4 to +0.5 defecations/d at weeks 2-4, attenuated by week 6, with less bloating OR 0.34 and more flatulence OR 2.62). The 2025 British Dietetic Association Chronic Constipation Guidelines (Dimidi 2025 PMID:41081381 / Van Der Schoot 2024 PMID:37905980; pooled n=48 rye vs white bread arms) issue a qualified recommendation that rye bread increases stool frequency (+0.43 BM/wk, 95% CI 0.03-0.83, low certainty), while explicitly preserving the strongest contrary tolerability signal: rye bread worsened the 0-18 composite global GI symptom score (+2.00 points, 95% CI 0.48-3.53; driven by fermentable fructans/gas/cramping, consistent with Laatikainen 2016 PMID:27417338 in IBS where regular rye caused more flatulence, pain, and cramps than low-FODMAP rye without altering constipation VAS p=0.66) and required 6-8 slices/day. Kept at minimal_signal (50.005) due to non-PD populations, baked rather than specifically toasted preparation, high dose requirement, and fructan/gluten tolerability caveats (contraindicated in celiac disease).

Direct clinical signal that dried saffron stigma powder eases rather than worsens anxiety in Parkinson's disease, contradicting the frozen 'worsens' hypothesis (Maybe False) and matching Round 1 direct_clinical_signal verdicts for saffron depression (0063) and fatigue (0485). Supporting non-PD DB-RCTs also show anxiety reductions (Mazidi 2016 n=54 BAI p<0.001; Kell 2017 n=128 Affron 28 mg; Lopresti 2018 n=68 youth RCADS; Milajerdi 2018 n=54 T2DM BAI p<0.05; Pouchieu 2023 acute MAST VAS anxiety). Minimal directional signal from non-PD Salvia officinalis clinical trials supporting the frozen 'reduces' anxiety hypothesis (Maybe True), calibrated consistently with Round 1 minimal_signal sage verdicts (0025 pain, 0060 insomnia, 0883 fatigue). Three oral S. officinalis trials provide partial non-PD anxiety signals: (1) Zeidabadi 2020 (PMC7114003; n=59 postmenopausal completers, 300 mg/day dry S. officinalis extract x 12 wk) reported significant reduction on the single MRS Anxiety item (2.13 -> 0.52 vs 2.00 -> 1.96, p<0.001; noting Table 2 Mean/SD reversal errors); (2) Dimpfel 2021 (PMC7881233; n=78 ITT / 48 PP postmenopausal women, fresh S. officinalis shoot-tip extract Menosan x 4 wk) significantly improved the MRS psychological domain vs placebo (p<0.05), though clinician-rated HAMA showed only a non-significant trend vs placebo; and (3) Kennedy 2006 (PMID:16205785; n=30 healthy crossover, 300/600 mg dried S. officinalis leaf) reduced pre-stressor STAI state anxiety at 300 mg (ABOLISHED during the DISS stressor) and raised calmness at 600 mg. Opposing/null evidence: Wightman 2021 (PMC7828691; n=94 Cognivia dual-species S. officinalis + S. lavandulaefolia EO bundle, 69% unblinding) found STAI state and trait anxiety COMPLETELY NULL! STRICT EXCLUSIONS: Spanish sage (S. lavandulaefolia) monotherapy trials (Tildesley 2005, Kennedy 2011) and synthetic neurosteroid SAGE-217/SAGE-718 trials are excluded. Safety caveats: alpha/beta-thujone GABA-A antagonism and seizure risk with concentrated sage oil or excessive ingestion (Lachenmeier 2010/2012; Rapino 2023), plus wide commercial supplement phytochemical variability (Maggini 2023).

In Scholey 2008 (PMID:18350281; n=20 healthy older adults, mean age 73 y, 5-period DB-PC crossover), a single 333 mg dose of standardized ethanolic S. officinalis extract significantly enhanced Accuracy of Attention and Secondary Memory vs placebo (p<0.05), whereas higher doses (666 and 1,332 mg) showed an inverted-U drop-off and Speed of Attention was unchanged. In Kennedy 2006 (PMID:16205785; n=30 healthy adults, dried S. officinalis leaf), 600 mg improved DISS multitasking performance whereas 300 mg REDUCED performance at 4 hours. Crucial opposing/null and direct-PD caveats: (1) the Newcastle PD-MCI dried S. officinalis leaf pilot (EudraCT 2007-002899-34; n=25 vs active Vitamin E) found NO overall cognitive advantage over Vitamin E (working-memory quality favored Vitamin E; isolated attention subscores unpublished); (2) Wightman 2021 (PMC7828691; n=94 Cognivia dual-species bundle, 69% unblinding) showed NO statistically significant attention improvement (Serial 3s/7s trends p=0.06-0.08 only); and (3) Spanish sage (S. lavandulaefolia) trials (Kennedy 2011; Tildesley 2005) are STRICTLY EXCLUDED as a different species (consistent with Round 1), as are synthetic SAGE-718/SAGE-217 drugs. Held strictly at minimal_signal (50.005). Safety caveats: thujone seizure neurotoxicity with sage oil/concentrates (Lachenmeier 2010/2012; Rapino 2023).

Safety caveats: major IgE-mediated food allergen capable of severe anaphylaxis (~0.1-0.2% prevalence; US FASTER Act 9th major allergen; Zhao 2026, PMID:41391419), colonic sesame seed phytobezoar/obstruction risk with heavy unchewed seed intake (Shaw 2007, PMID:18047637 — pertinent in PD slow-transit constipation), pregnancy/emmenagogue uterotonic hazard at medicinal doses (Aghababaei 2021, PMID:34192691), and dietary protein timing considerations if large tahini/seed portions are taken with levodopa.
